It does not assert the Lean theorem for all measurable independent variables satisfying only a one-point negative-Laplace bound; that premise admits genuine cases outside the source class, including atomic distributions.

rationale: The target preserves the exact small-sum event and bound of Exercise 2.2.10(b). Its key difference is principled and strengthening: instead of retaining the source's nonnegativity, continuity, and density-bound hypotheses, it assumes the negative-Laplace estimate that source part (a) proves at t = 1/ε. Hence every source instance is covered, while the Lean statement also applies to genuinely broader, satisfiable distribution classes. The index-type generalization is harmless, all 58 dependencies have standard intended semantics, and no unresolved item requires adjudication.
